spots.name: Choctaw National Wildlife Refuge
spots.tip: Wildlife is most active in the first two hours after sunrise. Stay on trails, use your car as a blind on auto routes and give animals space.

spots.name: Leaf River Bridge
spots.tip: A landmark bridge: try blue hour when the lights come on, or low side light that shows the structure.

spots.name: Choctaw NWR
spots.tip: eBird birding hotspot with 143 species recorded. Birds are most active in the first two hours after sunrise; recent sightings at ebird.org/hotspot/L919297.

spots.name: Old St. Stephens Historical Park
spots.tip: eBird birding hotspot with 118 species recorded. Birds are most active in the first two hours after sunrise; recent sightings at ebird.org/hotspot/L1042898.

spots.name: Silver Hill
spots.tip: A notable summit. Check the road and trail first; first and last light on high ground is the reason to go, and it's often the subject from below. Summit 86 m (282 ft).

spots.name: Quitman Lookout Tower
spots.tip: A lookout tower or fire lookout: a full-circle view, so it works at sunrise and sunset. Many are staffed in summer and some can be rented.

spots.name: Aquilla Lookout Tower
spots.tip: A lookout tower or fire lookout: a full-circle view, so it works at sunrise and sunset. Many are staffed in summer and some can be rented.

spots.name: Cedar Creek Falls
spots.tip: Best under soft overcast or in shade so the highlights don't blow out. A slow shutter (1/4–1 s on a tripod) smooths the water; flow peaks after rain and snowmelt.

spots.name: Longfield Sandbar
spots.tip: Low tide and wet sand give reflections at sunset. Check the tide table and never turn your back on the waves.
